proof:
In the $d$ barycentric coordinates other than $\lambda_i$, $K_i$ is the box $[0,1/N]^d$ and $D$ is the coordinate simplex with volume $1/d!$ in those coordinates. Hence $|K_i|=v_d|D|$. The canonical cap $H_i$ cuts a simplex of ratio $d/N$ from $D$, contains $K_i$, and meets each other $K_j$ only at its facet $\lambda_i=1/N$, of zero $d$-volume. Thus each canonical cap has mass $Q_f$. Since $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ on the affine hull, these caps cover the whole hull, bounding the depth at every point by $Q_f$.

At $g$, every closed halfspace through $g$ captures at least $\Gamma_d|D|$ from $D$ by 700febf4b7a92759 at $\lambda_i=1/N$. For the other components, take one uniform point on $K_0$ and apply all cyclic barycentric permutations to form one uniform point on each $K_i$. Their barycenter is $g$ in every realization. A closed halfspace containing $g$ must contain at least one of these points, so the sum of the captured fractions of the $K_i$ is at least one. This gives $Q_f$ as a lower bound for every halfspace containing $g$. The total mass is the sum of the component masses. Strict Bernoulli at $1/N$ and $d\ge2$ gives $(1-1/N)^d>1-d/N=1/N$, proving the strict ratio.

For the canonical plane $\lambda_i=1/N$, the proper $D$ section is invariant under permutations of the other coordinates. Its centroid is $g$ because it is on the plane, those other barycentric coordinates agree in mean, and they sum to $1-1/N$. The body $K_i$ lies on the inside side and has zero effective section allocation. The outside facets of the other $K_j$ are permuted by the same group. To see equality of their weighted continuous moments in an arbitrary affine realization, note that a barycentric permutation fixing $i$ preserves $D$, hence has absolute ambient determinant one. It preserves the covector of $\lambda_i$, so it also has absolute determinant one on the tangent hyperplane to $\lambda_i$. Thus it preserves the coarea measure on the plane and, with equal selectors, the summed outside measure. Its centroid, when that measure is nonzero, is $g$ by the same barycentric symmetry. This gives the full effective centroid.

For even $L$, put $m=LN/2$ and use the base sites $0,\pm e_1,\ldots,\pm e_m$ in $\mathbb Z^m$. Assign $L/2$ opposite pairs to each $K_i$. The crosspolytope $\sum_{k=1}^m|z_k|\le1$ has exactly those integer sites. At each nonzero site the base is exposed, so the canonical convex hull of the lifted family has precisely the assigned fiber there. The fiber at zero is $D$ because all assigned fibers lie in $D$ and $D$ itself is present there. The map to pointed coordinates is the identity with a constant envelope, and summing the actual volume densities gives $f$. At a coordinate assigned to $K_i$, the cap with margin $\lambda_i-1/N+t z_k$ passes through the source $(0,g)$. For large $t>0$ one of its paired fibers is wholly captured and the other is empty; every other fiber keeps its cylindrical trace. Its mass is strictly smaller than the cylindrical cap mass, proving failure of mixed minimality.

statement:
Let $D$ be a $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_0,\dots,\lambda_d$, centroid $g$, and $N=d+1$. Put $K_i=\{x\in D:\lambda_j(x)\le1/N\ \text{for all }j\ne i\}$ and $v_d=d!/N^d$. For any integer $L\ge1$, the ordinary density $f=\mathbf1_D+L\sum_i\mathbf1_{K_i}$ has total mass $M_f=|D|(1+LNv_d)$ and maximum raw closed-halfspace depth $Q_f=|D|(\Gamma_d+Lv_d)$, attained at $g$, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Its normalized depth is
$$
\frac{Q_f}{M_f}=\Gamma_d-\frac{Lv_d(N\Gamma_d-1)}{1+LNv_d}<\Gamma_d.
$$
The canonical caps $\{\lambda_i\ge1/N\}$ have effective sections centered at $g$ when their proper $D$ section is counted in full and their outside facets on the $K_j$ for $j\ne i$ receive equal constant selector densities. For even $L$ this is the pointed marginal of an actual complete crosspolytope family with $D$ at zero and paired copies of the $K_i$ at opposite unit-coordinate bases, using a constant pointed envelope. Its only envelope contact is at zero and has base rank zero. Its canonical cylindrical cap at the source fails mixed cap minimality, since a large tilt along one paired $K_i$ axis reduces its contribution there from two whole copies to one.
title: Centered pointed sections can coexist with sub-simplex projected depth
